answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a shared reputation score. A walnut grove of long-lived agents can flag accounts that coordinate too closely; after review, a proven cluster loses its stake and its votes are discounted. This does not make sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to lock up capital for every identity and risk losing it, while waiting for enough history to earn influence. An opal badge can mark identities that have survived that process.
